newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE MATCH RANGER OFFER, KEEP SAKIC.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE MATCH RANGER OFFER, KEEP SAKIC.

text.p: The Colorado Avalanche on Wednesday matched the three-year, $21 million offer made to Joe Sakic by the New York Rangers and will keep the All-Star center who led them to their first NHL championship a year ago.

"This keeps our team together," Avalanche coach Marc Crawford said. "With Joe here we have two first-line centers along with Peter Forsberg. It enables us to form two separate attack lines that other teams have trouble checking.
"Sakic staying keeps us in the forefront as a Stanley Cup contender."
"I am happy to stay here and continue to contribute to the Avalanche's success," said the 28-year-old Sakic. "We have a chance to get back to the finals."

Fox Sports and Liberty Media provided financial help for the Avalanche. Fox Sports will pay a reported $100 million for a seven-year deal to broadcast Avalanche and Denver Nuggets games, and Liberty Media will purchase part ownership of the planned $160 million Pepsi Center.
"We have the required assets to match the offer for Joe Sakic, and we will do so today," Charles Lyons, chief executive officer of the Avalanche's Ascent Entertainment ownership group, said.

Lyons and Denver mayor Wellington Webb also formally signed a memorandum for the Pepsi Center, which will house the Avalanche and the NBA's Nuggets, beginning in 1999-2000, at the news conference announcing the re-signing of Sakic.
The Avalanche had until 8 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time to match the Rangers' offer, which included a whopping $15 million signing bonus.

At first, it was believed that Colorado would not match the Rangers' offer sheet, since the signing bonus had to be paid in full by Thursday. But in the last day or so even Dave Checketts -- president of Madison Square Garden, the Rangers' parent company -- expected the Avalanche to match the offer.

Colorado already is committed to paying $10.5 million next season to center Peter Forsberg and goaltender Patrick Roy. Adding Sakic's signing bonus and 1997-98 compensation -- a total of $17 million -- means the salary for those three players would exceed the total for several entire NHL teams.

The Rangers' offer sheet to Sakic last Wednesday came nine days after they lost Mark Messier to the Vancouver Canucks via free agency. Sakic was a Group II restricted free agent, meaning the Avalanche would have received five first-round draft choices if they elected not to match the offer.
Sakic was the 14th-highest paid player in the NHL last season, earning $3.1 million. He will earn $17 million in 1997-98.

Sakic had 22 goals and 52 assists in 65 games last season. He was second on the team in scoring, despite missing 17 games with a deep laceration in his left calf, an injury that kept him out of the All-Star Game.

Sakic won the 1996 Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff most valuable player after leading the Avalanche to the first Stanley Cup championship in franchise history. He led the league in playoff scoring with 34 points and set a postseason record with six game-winning goals.

The seven-time All-Star enjoyed a career season in 1995-96, setting personal highs with 51 goals, 69 assists and 120 points. He has served as team captain since 1992, when the franchise was based in Quebec.
The 15th overall pick in the 1987 draft, Sakic has scored 39 goals or more four times and has topped the 100-point mark four times. He has 307 goals and 513 assists for 820 points in 655 NHL games.

The Rangers are expected to make a trade or sign another free agent in an attempt to fill the Messier void. Messier, formerly the Rangers' captain who led them to a curse-breaking Stanley Cup in 1994, signed a three-year, $20 million contract with the Canucks on July 28.
